status_note: PROPOSED, EXPERIMENTAL and OPT-IN. Not required by draft-pidlisnyi-aps-03, whose section 3.3 rules one revocation result per chain member and closes chain verification at valid, invalid, indeterminate and unsupported. Draft-03 says nothing about two sources answering about the same member, nothing about a per-source freshness bound, nothing about coverage over a declared source set and nothing about an offline admission on a snapshot. Concept source: the aeoess/agent-authority-lifecycle concept document, invariant L7 and invariant candidate BROAD-L7. Nothing downstream should bind to these names as specified text.
description: Cross-language parity vectors for the multi-source status decision: per-source freshness bounds, conflict between accepted sources, coverage over a declared required set, and an offline admission on a snapshot inside a declared bound. The TypeScript and Python SDKs must produce identical results for every case. Expectations are hand specified here and are never computed by the code under test.
coverage_limb_is_not_completeness: The coverage block reports whether every member of a DECLARED required-source set produced a usable determinate answer. It is not a completeness claim. Invariant L12 is open and nothing in these vectors answers it. complete true must not be read as a statement that the declared set was every source that mattered.
unresolved_questions_the_vectors_pin_rat: What a conflict returns. SC-04 and SC-05 are the same inputs under the two readings, and only the boundary outcome moves.
Whether an answer past its own bound still counts. SC-06 and SC-07 are the same inputs under the two readings, and the verdicts are opposite.
What a silent required source means. SC-09 and SC-10 are the same inputs under the two readings, and one admits where the other does not.

decision_cases.tests: The admit path before any disagreement. One required source, one answer inside the bound declared for it, active.
Both required sources answer active inside their own bounds. Coverage is complete over the declared set and the used states agree, which is the only shape that admits online.
Agreement on revoked is not a conflict. The artifact verdict is invalid and the reason says revoked rather than conflict.

Two accepted sources, both inside their own bounds, disagree. Under deny_with_conflict the boundary denies. The ARTIFACT verdict is not_established with the source limb, never invalid: a conflict is the verifier reaching no conclusion, not a finding that the authority ended.

The same conflict under the other reading the proposed text permits. Only the BOUNDARY outcome moves, to not_established. The artifact verdict, the reason code and the conflict block are identical, which is why the policy is a required parameter rather than a default.

The deployment-relevant case, first reading. A revoked answer past its own bound against a fresh active one. With stale_revoked_still_counts set, the revoked answer is still used and the states conflict, so the boundary denies.

The same inputs under the other reading. With stale_revoked_still_counts clear, the revoked answer is dropped past its bound, one fresh active answer remains and coverage over the declared set is short. The verdicts are opposite, which is the whole reason the module refuses a default.

Both sources answer active and one answer is older than the bound declared for it. The stale answer is not false and it is not a revocation. It establishes nothing, so the boundary is not_established rather than admit or deny.

A required source produced no observation at all. Under silence_is coverage_gap, coverage is measured over the declared set, so the answers that did arrive cannot cover it. The reason says coverage, which is a different finding from a stale answer.

The same silence under the other reading. Coverage is measured over the sources that answered, so the boundary admits. The silent source is still named in the record, so the two readings can be told apart afterwards.

One source answers past its bound and the other answers unavailable. Nothing usable and determinate remains, and the reason distinguishes that from a stale answer inside a covered set and from a silent source. All three limbs are missing at once and all three are reported.

A verifier that declared itself offline in advance, with a snapshot inside the bound it declared, may admit. BROAD-L7 does not require liveness. The record names the snapshot it admitted on and the age that snapshot had at the boundary, so the admission can be recomputed from the record alone.
The same offline verifier with a snapshot older than the bound it declared. The declared bound is the entire basis for the offline admission, so past it the snapshot establishes nothing.

The offline verifier holds a snapshot inside its declared bound saying revoked. Being offline is a reason to admit less, never a reason to soften an observed revocation, so the revoked branch runs before the offline branch.
Offline mode with no answer from the declared snapshot source at all. The source limb is missing, not the freshness limb: nothing was too old, there was nothing.

The answer is exactly as old as the bound declared for its source. The comparison is inclusive, so this admits. Paired with SC-17 so which side of the boundary each verdict sits on is pinned rather than assumed.
One second older than SC-16 and the only source in the trust policy. Nothing usable remains. The answer still says active and nothing here calls it false.

A second authorization boundary ten minutes after SC-02, where one source now reports revoked. It is a new decision at a new boundary. It says nothing about the earlier record and never rewrites it, which the test asserts separately by holding the earlier result and comparing it after this one is computed.

BROAD-L7's source limb. An answer from a source the trust policy does not name is not an input to the verdict, whatever it says. It is still recorded, with a null bound and use_basis source_not_accepted, so a reader can see it arrived and was not used.

An answer whose as_of is later than the boundary instant. No age against the declared bound is measurable, so the answer is refused rather than read as fresh. The basis records it as skew rather than as staleness, because the proposed text does not rule clock skew at all and the two are different findings.

The weakest posture the module can be put in, pinned so it is visible in a record. With stale_active_still_counts set, an active answer past its own bound is used and the boundary admits. within_bound stays false and the use basis names the policy that admitted it, so nobody can read this record as a fresh observation.

One accepted source answers revoked inside its bound and the other required source is silent. An observed revocation from an accepted source does not need a complete source set to count, so the boundary denies rather than returning a coverage gap.

Every required source was consulted and none produced a usable answer. The freshness limb is not missing, because nothing was measured against a bound. Unknown status is not active and it is not revoked.

An offline verifier whose snapshot says active while a required source it did reach says revoked, both inside their own bounds. The conflict branch runs before the offline branch, so there is no admission and no snapshot block.

error_cases.tests: silence_is has no default. The two readings decide whether a silent required source blocks an admission and the text as written supports both.
A verifier that accepts no source for a claim cannot establish it, so an empty declared set is refused rather than read as vacuously covered.
conflict_policy has no default. A default would be the module ruling a question the proposed text leaves open.
stale_policy has no default and both members are required.
There are two verifier modes and a third is not read as one of them.
Offline mode with no declared snapshot source. BROAD-L7 forbids admitting on a snapshot with no declared bound, and this makes that state unreachable rather than merely discouraged.
A snapshot source in online mode is meaningless and is refused rather than silently ignored.
One source id carrying two different declared bounds has no answer to which bound applies.
The same source declared twice with different bounds is ambiguous.
Two answers from one source is a disagreement inside a source rather than between two, which is not the question this module decides.
The answer set is closed at active, revoked and unavailable. An unrecognised answer is refused rather than mapped onto one of them.
An unavailable answer dates nothing, so an as_of on one is a defect in the call rather than a fact about the authority.
An unparseable boundary instant is a programming error, not a verdict. Returning not_established here would report ignorance about the authority when the defect is in the call.
A negative freshness bound is not a bound.
The decision is about one named authority and an unnamed one cannot be recorded.
A determinate answer with no as_of cannot be aged against any bound, so it is refused rather than admitted as fresh.
